“Sir,” I said, “I do not understand at all the period of deception, pleasure, and torment. Please explain it to me more clearly.”

He answered me, “Your foolishness continues. You refuse to purify your heart and serve God. Be careful, or time may run out and you may be found foolish. So listen, as you wish, so that you can understand these things.

“A person who takes pleasure and is deceived for even one day, doing whatever he wants, covers himself with great foolishness. He does not understand what he is doing, and the next day he forgets what he did the day before. Pleasure and deception have no memory because of the foolishness he has put on. But when punishment and torment cling to someone for one day, that person will be punished and tormented for up to a year, because punishment and torment have a long memory.

“So, while he is tormented and punished for a whole year, he eventually remembers his pleasure and the deception. He realizes that he suffers these evils because of them. Everyone who takes pleasure and is deceived is tormented in this way because, although they have life, they have given themselves over to death.”

“Sir,” I asked, “what kinds of pleasure are harmful?”

He says, “Every act that a person takes pleasure in is a form of pleasure. A hot-tempered person takes pleasure by letting his anger have all it wants. In the same way, adulterers, drunkards, slanderers, liars, greedy people, cheats, and all who do similar things feed their own disease and take pleasure in what they do. All such pleasures harm God’s servants. Therefore, those who are punished and tormented suffer because of these deceptions.

“But there are also pleasures that save people. For many people take pleasure in doing good and are carried along by the pleasure they find in it. This kind of pleasure benefits the servants of God and secures life for such a person. But the harmful pleasures mentioned earlier bring torment and punishment. If people persist in them and do not repent[a], they bring death on themselves.”

translation:
  text: '“Sir,” I said, “I do not understand at all the period of deception, pleasure, and torment. Please
    explain it to me more clearly.”


    He answered me, “Your foolishness continues. You refuse to purify your heart and serve God. Be careful,
    or time may run out and you may be found foolish. So listen, as you wish, so that you can understand
    these things.


    “A person who takes pleasure and is deceived for even one day, doing whatever he wants, covers himself
    with great foolishness. He does not understand what he is doing, and the next day he forgets what
    he did the day before. Pleasure and deception have no memory because of the foolishness he has put
    on. But when punishment and torment cling to someone for one day, that person will be punished and
    tormented for up to a year, because punishment and torment have a long memory.


    “So, while he is tormented and punished for a whole year, he eventually remembers his pleasure and
    the deception. He realizes that he suffers these evils because of them. Everyone who takes pleasure
    and is deceived is tormented in this way because, although they have life, they have given themselves
    over to death.”


    “Sir,” I asked, “what kinds of pleasure are harmful?”


    He says, “Every act that a person takes pleasure in is a form of pleasure. A hot-tempered person takes
    pleasure by letting his anger have all it wants. In the same way, adulterers, drunkards, slanderers,
    liars, greedy people, cheats, and all who do similar things feed their own disease and take pleasure
    in what they do. All such pleasures harm God’s servants. Therefore, those who are punished and tormented
    suffer because of these deceptions.


    “But there are also pleasures that save people. For many people take pleasure in doing good and are
    carried along by the pleasure they find in it. This kind of pleasure benefits the servants of God
    and secures life for such a person. But the harmful pleasures mentioned earlier bring torment and
    punishment. If people persist in them and do not repent[a], they bring death on themselves.”'
